title: Se7en
starring: Brad Pitt, Morgan Freeman, Gwyneth Paltrow, Kevin Spacey
honours: Oscar nom for Best Film Editing
head: Se7en
craze: Its rain-soaked dread and gut-punch finale rewired the serial-killer thriller. The 'What's in the box?' ending is still one of the most quoted, debated twists in film history.
rows: Brad Pitt, Morgan Freeman, Gwyneth Paltrow, Kevin Spacey
Oscar nom for Best Film Editing
dyk: Kevin Spacey was left out of the opening credits to keep the killer's reveal a surprise.

title: The Game
starring: Michael Douglas, Sean Penn, Deborah Kara Unger, James Rebhorn
head: The Game
craze: A paranoid puzzle box where reality keeps folding in on itself, it rewards viewers who love being kept off balance. Fans revisit it to spot how every clue was planted in plain sight.
rows: Michael Douglas, Sean Penn, Deborah Kara Unger, James Rebhorn
dyk: Fincher's follow-up to Se7en; the script by John Brancato and Michael Ferris circulated for years before it.

title: Fight Club
starring: Brad Pitt, Edward Norton, Helena Bonham Carter, Meat Loaf
honours: Oscar nom for Best Sound Effects Editing
head: Fight Club
craze: A box-office disappointment that became a generation's cult manifesto, it skewers consumerism and masculinity with savage wit. Its rules, twist and Tyler Durden quotes are endlessly memed and argued over.
rows: Brad Pitt, Edward Norton, Helena Bonham Carter, Meat Loaf
Oscar nom for Best Sound Effects Editing
dyk: Adapted from Chuck Palahniuk's 1996 debut novel; it underperformed in theaters before exploding on DVD.

title: Panic Room
starring: Jodie Foster, Kristen Stewart, Forest Whitaker, Dwight Yoakam
head: Panic Room
craze: A tight, single-location pressure cooker with a camera that glides through walls and keyholes. It's a masterclass in sustained tension and an early showcase for a young Kristen Stewart.
rows: Jodie Foster, Kristen Stewart, Forest Whitaker, Dwight Yoakam
dyk: Nicole Kidman was originally cast but left after a knee injury; Jodie Foster stepped in.

title: Zodiac
starring: Jake Gyllenhaal, Mark Ruffalo, Robert Downey Jr., Anthony Edwards
honours: Competed for the Palme d'Or at Cannes 2007
head: Zodiac
craze: A meticulous portrait of obsession that refuses easy answers, it grows richer with every rewatch. Many now rank it as Fincher's masterpiece and one of the best films of the 2000s.
rows: Jake Gyllenhaal, Mark Ruffalo, Robert Downey Jr., Anthony Edwards
Competed for the Palme d'Or at Cannes 2007
dyk: One of the first major features shot largely digitally, on the Thomson Viper camera.

title: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
starring: Brad Pitt, Cate Blanchett, Taraji P. Henson, Tilda Swinton
honours: Won 3 Oscars from 13 nominations
head: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
craze: A sweeping, melancholy love story about time slipping away, built on landmark digital-aging effects. Its quiet meditation on mortality has made it a tearjerker staple for many viewers.
rows: Brad Pitt, Cate Blanchett, Taraji P. Henson, Tilda Swinton
dyk: Loosely based on F. Scott Fitzgerald's 1922 short story of a man who ages in reverse.

title: The Social Network
starring: Jesse Eisenberg, Andrew Garfield, Justin Timberlake, Armie Hammer
honours: Won 3 Oscars incl. Adapted Screenplay; Golden Globe for Best Drama
head: The Social Network
craze: Sorkin's rapid-fire dialogue and Reznor-Ross's pulsing score turned Facebook's origin into a modern tragedy. It's often called the defining film about tech, ambition and betrayal of its era.
rows: Jesse Eisenberg, Andrew Garfield, Justin Timberlake, Armie Hammer
Won 3 Oscars incl. Adapted Screenplay; Golden Globe for Best Drama
dyk: The opening breakup scene reportedly took 99 takes to get right.

title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
starring: Daniel Craig, Rooney Mara, Christopher Plummer, Stellan Skarsgård
honours: Won Oscar for Best Film Editing; Rooney Mara nominated for Best Actress
head: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
craze: A cold, chic adaptation of Stieg Larsson's bestseller that leans into its icy Swedish atmosphere. Rooney Mara's fierce, transformative Lisbeth is what keeps fans coming back.
rows: Daniel Craig, Rooney Mara, Christopher Plummer, Stellan Skarsgård
Won Oscar for Best Film Editing; Rooney Mara nominated for Best Actress
dyk: Rooney Mara got pierced and bleached her eyebrows for the role of Lisbeth Salander.

title: Gone Girl
starring: Ben Affleck, Rosamund Pike, Neil Patrick Harris, Tyler Perry
honours: Rosamund Pike nominated for the Best Actress Oscar
head: Gone Girl
craze: A darkly funny dissection of marriage and media spectacle with a mid-film rug pull audiences still talk about. Pike's 'Cool Girl' monologue became a cultural touchstone.
rows: Ben Affleck, Rosamund Pike, Neil Patrick Harris, Tyler Perry
Rosamund Pike nominated for the Best Actress Oscar
dyk: Gillian Flynn adapted her own novel; it became Fincher's highest-grossing film.

title: Mank
starring: Gary Oldman, Amanda Seyfried, Lily Collins, Tom Pelphrey
honours: Won 2 Oscars from a leading 10 nominations
head: Mank
craze: A black-and-white love letter to old Hollywood, styled like a 1940s film, about the making of Citizen Kane. Cinephiles relish its period craft and backstage politics.
rows: Gary Oldman, Amanda Seyfried, Lily Collins, Tom Pelphrey
Won 2 Oscars from a leading 10 nominations
dyk: The screenplay was written by Fincher's late father, Jack Fincher, decades before it was filmed.

title: The Killer
starring: Michael Fassbender, Tilda Swinton, Charles Parnell, Arliss Howard
honours: Competed for the Golden Lion at Venice 2023
head: The Killer
craze: A precise, deadpan character study of a hitman whose perfect routine unravels after one miss. Fans love its dry humor, Smiths-heavy soundtrack and clinical style.
rows: Michael Fassbender, Tilda Swinton, Charles Parnell, Arliss Howard
Competed for the Golden Lion at Venice 2023
dyk: Based on the French graphic novel series by Alexis 'Matz' Nolent and Luc Jacamon.

title: Mean Streets
starring: Harvey Keitel, Robert De Niro, David Proval, Amy Robinson
honours: De Niro won NSFC and NYFCC Best Supporting Actor
head: Mean Streets
craze: The raw, rock-scored street film where Scorsese's voice first came fully alive. Its blend of Catholic guilt, small-time crime and pop music set the template for decades of gangster cinema.
rows: Harvey Keitel, Robert De Niro, David Proval, Amy Robinson
De Niro won NSFC and NYFCC Best Supporting Actor
dyk: Scorsese's first collaboration with Robert De Niro; added to the National Film Registry in 1997.

title: Taxi Driver
starring: Robert De Niro, Jodie Foster, Cybill Shepherd, Harvey Keitel
honours: Won the Palme d'Or; 4 Oscar noms incl. Best Picture
head: Taxi Driver
craze: A feverish descent into urban loneliness that made Travis Bickle an enduring, unsettling icon. Its influence runs through countless films about alienated men, including Joker.
rows: Robert De Niro, Jodie Foster, Cybill Shepherd, Harvey Keitel
Won the Palme d'Or; 4 Oscar noms incl. Best Picture
dyk: De Niro's famous 'You talkin' to me?' mirror scene was largely improvised.

title: Raging Bull
starring: Robert De Niro, Cathy Moriarty, Joe Pesci
honours: Won 2 Oscars incl. Best Actor (De Niro) from 8 nominations
head: Raging Bull
craze: Shot in stark black and white, its brutal fight scenes and self-destructive hero redefined the sports biopic. It routinely appears near the top of all-time greatest film lists.
rows: Robert De Niro, Cathy Moriarty, Joe Pesci
Won 2 Oscars incl. Best Actor (De Niro) from 8 nominations
dyk: De Niro gained roughly 60 pounds to play the older Jake LaMotta.

title: The King of Comedy
starring: Robert De Niro, Jerry Lewis, Sandra Bernhard
honours: Won BAFTA for Best Original Screenplay
head: The King of Comedy
craze: An uncomfortably funny satire of celebrity obsession that feels more prophetic every year. Rupert Pupkin's desperate hunger for fame now reads like a preview of the influencer age.
rows: Robert De Niro, Jerry Lewis, Sandra Bernhard
Won BAFTA for Best Original Screenplay
dyk: A box-office flop on release, it later became a major inspiration for 2019's Joker.

title: Goodfellas
starring: Robert De Niro, Ray Liotta, Joe Pesci, Lorraine Bracco
honours: Won Oscar for Supporting Actor (Pesci); BAFTA Best Film
head: Goodfellas
craze: Its kinetic energy, freeze-frames and wall-to-wall soundtrack made mob life look thrilling and then terrifying. Lines like 'Funny how?' made it the most quoted gangster film of its generation.
rows: Robert De Niro, Ray Liotta, Joe Pesci, Lorraine Bracco
Won Oscar for Supporting Actor (Pesci); BAFTA Best Film
dyk: The Copacabana entrance is a single unbroken Steadicam shot lasting about three minutes.

title: Cape Fear
starring: Robert De Niro, Nick Nolte, Jessica Lange, Juliette Lewis
honours: 2 Oscar noms (De Niro, Juliette Lewis)
head: Cape Fear
craze: De Niro's tattooed, cackling Max Cady is one of cinema's most menacing villains. Scorsese's operatic, Hitchcock-style flourishes turned a genre remake into a big hit.
rows: Robert De Niro, Nick Nolte, Jessica Lange, Juliette Lewis
dyk: Remake of the 1962 film; original stars Gregory Peck and Robert Mitchum appear in cameos.

title: Casino
starring: Robert De Niro, Sharon Stone, Joe Pesci, James Woods
honours: Sharon Stone won a Golden Globe and earned an Oscar nom
head: Casino
craze: A dazzling, detailed autopsy of how the mob ran Vegas and then lost it. Fans love its narration-driven sweep, Stone's ferocious turn and Pesci at his most volatile.
rows: Robert De Niro, Sharon Stone, Joe Pesci, James Woods
Sharon Stone won a Golden Globe and earned an Oscar nom
dyk: Based on Nicholas Pileggi's nonfiction book about mob-run Las Vegas casinos.

title: Gangs of New York
starring: Leonardo DiCaprio, Daniel Day-Lewis, Cameron Diaz, Jim Broadbent
honours: 10 Oscar nominations incl. Best Picture
head: Gangs of New York
craze: Daniel Day-Lewis's Bill the Butcher is a towering, much-imitated villain. The film also launched the long Scorsese-DiCaprio partnership.
rows: Leonardo DiCaprio, Daniel Day-Lewis, Cameron Diaz, Jim Broadbent
dyk: Its 1860s Manhattan streets were built as massive sets at Cinecittà Studios in Rome.

title: The Aviator
starring: Leonardo DiCaprio, Cate Blanchett, Kate Beckinsale, John C. Reilly
honours: Won 5 Oscars incl. Supporting Actress (Blanchett) from 11 noms
head: The Aviator
craze: A lavish portrait of Howard Hughes's genius and unraveling mind, with spectacular aviation set pieces. DiCaprio's intense performance marked his arrival as a serious leading man.
rows: Leonardo DiCaprio, Cate Blanchett, Kate Beckinsale, John C. Reilly
Won 5 Oscars incl. Supporting Actress (Blanchett) from 11 noms
dyk: Cate Blanchett won an Oscar for playing Katharine Hepburn, herself a four-time Oscar winner.

title: The Departed
starring: Leonardo DiCaprio, Matt Damon, Jack Nicholson, Mark Wahlberg
honours: Won 4 Oscars incl. Best Picture and Best Director
head: The Departed
craze: A twisty cat-and-mouse game of moles with an all-star cast firing on every cylinder. Its shock ending and Boston swagger made it Scorsese's long-awaited crowning win.
rows: Leonardo DiCaprio, Matt Damon, Jack Nicholson, Mark Wahlberg
Won 4 Oscars incl. Best Picture and Best Director
dyk: A remake of the 2002 Hong Kong thriller Infernal Affairs; it won Scorsese his first Oscar.

title: Shutter Island
starring: Leonardo DiCaprio, Mark Ruffalo, Ben Kingsley, Michelle Williams
head: Shutter Island
craze: A gothic mind-bender whose final line sparks endless debate about what Teddy really knew. Viewers rewatch it to catch the clues hidden in nearly every scene.
rows: Leonardo DiCaprio, Mark Ruffalo, Ben Kingsley, Michelle Williams
dyk: Adapted from Dennis Lehane's 2003 novel of the same name.

title: The Wolf of Wall Street
starring: Leonardo DiCaprio, Jonah Hill, Margot Robbie, Matthew McConaughey
honours: 5 Oscar noms incl. Best Picture; DiCaprio won the Golden Globe
head: The Wolf of Wall Street
craze: An outrageous, three-hour roller coaster of greed and excess that made Jordan Belfort a meme. McConaughey's chest-thump and the Quaalude scene became instant pop-culture landmarks.
rows: Leonardo DiCaprio, Jonah Hill, Margot Robbie, Matthew McConaughey
5 Oscar noms incl. Best Picture; DiCaprio won the Golden Globe
dyk: It set a Guinness record for the most swearing in a motion picture.

title: Silence
starring: Andrew Garfield, Adam Driver, Liam Neeson, Tadanobu Asano
honours: Oscar nom for Best Cinematography
head: Silence
craze: A searching, deeply personal meditation on faith and doubt set amid persecution in 17th-century Japan. Many fans see it as the spiritual key to Scorsese's whole body of work.
rows: Andrew Garfield, Adam Driver, Liam Neeson, Tadanobu Asano
dyk: Scorsese spent nearly three decades trying to adapt Shūsaku Endō's 1966 novel.

title: The Irishman
starring: Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci, Harvey Keitel
honours: 10 Oscar nominations incl. Best Picture
head: The Irishman
craze: A somber, elegiac look back at a life in the mob, reuniting screen legends one last time. Its quiet, devastating final hour turned a gangster epic into a meditation on regret.
rows: Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci, Harvey Keitel
dyk: Joe Pesci came out of semi-retirement for the role; the actors were digitally de-aged.

title: Killers of the Flower Moon
starring: Leonardo DiCaprio, Lily Gladstone, Robert De Niro, Jesse Plemons
honours: 10 Oscar noms; Lily Gladstone won the Golden Globe for Best Actress
head: Killers of the Flower Moon
craze: It brought a buried chapter of American history to a global audience. Lily Gladstone's quietly powerful performance was widely celebrated as historic.
rows: Leonardo DiCaprio, Lily Gladstone, Robert De Niro, Jesse Plemons
10 Oscar noms; Lily Gladstone won the Golden Globe for Best Actress
dyk: Based on David Grann's 2017 nonfiction book about the Osage murders of the 1920s.

title: Arjun Reddy
starring: Vijay Deverakonda, Shalini Pandey, Rahul Ramakrishna, Jia Sharma
honours: Filmfare Award South for Best Actor (Vijay Deverakonda)
head: Arjun Reddy
craze: Its raw, unfiltered take on heartbreak and rage broke Telugu cinema conventions and turned Vijay Deverakonda into a star. It sparked fierce debates over its flawed hero and became a cult youth phenomenon.
rows: Vijay Deverakonda, Shalini Pandey, Rahul Ramakrishna, Jia Sharma
Filmfare Award South for Best Actor (Vijay Deverakonda)
dyk: Made on a budget of about ₹5 crore, it was remade in Hindi (Kabir Singh) and Tamil.

title: Kabir Singh
starring: Shahid Kapoor, Kiara Advani, Soham Majumdar, Arjan Bajwa
honours: IIFA Best Film and Best Actor (Shahid Kapoor)
head: Kabir Singh
craze: A Hindi remake of Arjun Reddy that became Shahid Kapoor's biggest solo hit. Its chart-topping songs like 'Bekhayali' and its polarizing hero kept it in headlines for months.
rows: Shahid Kapoor, Kiara Advani, Soham Majumdar, Arjan Bajwa
IIFA Best Film and Best Actor (Shahid Kapoor)
dyk: The first A-certified Indian film to gross over ₹200 crore in India.

title: Animal
starring: Ranbir Kapoor, Anil Kapoor, Bobby Deol, Rashmika Mandanna
honours: Filmfare Best Actor (Ranbir); 2 National Awards incl. Background Music
head: Animal
craze: A blood-soaked father-son saga that became a massive, divisive blockbuster. Bobby Deol's wordless villain entrance and the 'Jamal Kudu' song exploded across social media.
rows: Ranbir Kapoor, Anil Kapoor, Bobby Deol, Rashmika Mandanna
Filmfare Best Actor (Ranbir); 2 National Awards incl. Background Music
dyk: One of the highest-grossing A-rated Indian films ever, despite a runtime over three hours.

title: Dawn of the Dead
starring: Sarah Polley, Ving Rhames, Jake Weber, Mekhi Phifer
head: Dawn of the Dead
craze: This remake of Romero's classic swapped shamblers for sprinting zombies and a pulse-pounding pace. Its brilliant opening sequence is still hailed as one of the best in modern horror.
rows: Sarah Polley, Ving Rhames, Jake Weber, Mekhi Phifer
dyk: Snyder's feature debut; the screenplay was written by James Gunn.

starring: Gerard Butler, Lena Headey, David Wenham, Dominic West
craze: Its stylized slow-motion battles and 'This is Sparta!' roar became instant pop-culture shorthand. It also set off a wave of gym workouts and parodies.
rows: Gerard Butler, Lena Headey, David Wenham, Dominic West
dyk: Shot almost entirely against bluescreen, adapting Frank Miller's graphic novel panel by panel.

title: Watchmen
starring: Malin Åkerman, Billy Crudup, Matthew Goode, Jackie Earle Haley
head: Watchmen
craze: A faithful, dark deconstruction of superheroes that was ahead of its time. Rorschach and its haunting opening-credits montage keep it a cult favorite.
rows: Malin Åkerman, Billy Crudup, Matthew Goode, Jackie Earle Haley
dyk: Adapted from Alan Moore and Dave Gibbons' comic, long branded 'unfilmable' by Hollywood.

title: Man of Steel
starring: Henry Cavill, Amy Adams, Michael Shannon, Kevin Costner
head: Man of Steel
craze: A grounded, sci-fi reboot that launched the DC Extended Universe and Henry Cavill's beloved Superman. Its epic flight scene and Hans Zimmer theme still give fans chills.
rows: Henry Cavill, Amy Adams, Michael Shannon, Kevin Costner
dyk: Produced by Christopher Nolan, who co-developed the story with David S. Goyer.

title: Batman v Superman
starring: Ben Affleck, Henry Cavill, Amy Adams, Jesse Eisenberg
head: Batman v Superman
craze: The long-dreamed clash of DC's biggest icons drew huge crowds and fiercely split opinion. Affleck's brutal Batman and the warehouse fight remain fan favorites.
rows: Ben Affleck, Henry Cavill, Amy Adams, Jesse Eisenberg
dyk: Gal Gadot made her screen debut as Wonder Woman here, a year before her solo film.

title: Zack Snyder’s Justice League
starring: Ben Affleck, Henry Cavill, Gal Gadot, Ezra Miller
head: Zack Snyder’s Justice League
craze: A rare case of fans willing a director's vision into existence, delivered as a four-hour, 4:3 epic. Its richer arcs for Cyborg and Darkseid made it a vindication for Snyder loyalists.
rows: Ben Affleck, Henry Cavill, Gal Gadot, Ezra Miller
dyk: Released on HBO Max after years of the fan-driven #ReleaseTheSnyderCut campaign.

title: Army of the Dead
starring: Dave Bautista, Ella Purnell, Omari Hardwick, Ana de la Reguera
head: Army of the Dead
craze: A gleeful mix of heist caper and zombie carnage set in a ruined Las Vegas. It marked Snyder's playful return to the undead and spawned a Netflix franchise.
rows: Dave Bautista, Ella Purnell, Omari Hardwick, Ana de la Reguera
dyk: Tig Notaro's scenes were shot after principal photography and digitally inserted to replace another actor.

title: The Shawshank Redemption
starring: Tim Robbins, Morgan Freeman, Bob Gunton, William Sadler
honours: 7 Oscar nominations incl. Best Picture
head: The Shawshank Redemption
craze: A modest box-office performer that became the world's favorite film through TV and home video. Its message of hope and friendship has made it a comfort watch across generations.
rows: Tim Robbins, Morgan Freeman, Bob Gunton, William Sadler
dyk: Based on Stephen King's novella 'Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption'; it has long topped IMDb's Top 250.

title: The Green Mile
starring: Tom Hanks, Michael Clarke Duncan, David Morse, Bonnie Hunt
honours: 4 Oscar noms incl. Best Picture
head: The Green Mile
craze: A deeply emotional tale of compassion and injustice on death row. Michael Clarke Duncan's gentle John Coffey has moved audiences to tears for decades.
rows: Tom Hanks, Michael Clarke Duncan, David Morse, Bonnie Hunt
dyk: Stephen King first published the novel in six monthly paperback installments in 1996.

title: Shiva
starring: Nagarjuna, Amala, Raghuvaran, J. D. Chakravarthy
honours: Filmfare South Best Telugu Film; Nandi Award for Best Director
head: Shiva
craze: Its realistic college-gang violence and the iconic bicycle-chain fight transformed Telugu filmmaking. It made Nagarjuna a mass hero and launched a generation of filmmakers.
rows: Nagarjuna, Amala, Raghuvaran, J. D. Chakravarthy
Filmfare South Best Telugu Film; Nandi Award for Best Director
dyk: Varma's debut; it is credited with introducing the Steadicam to Telugu cinema.

title: Rangeela
starring: Aamir Khan, Urmila Matondkar, Jackie Shroff, Gulshan Grover
honours: Won 7 Filmfare Awards incl. Best Music (A. R. Rahman)
head: Rangeela
craze: A vibrant, breezy love triangle set in the film industry that made Urmila Matondkar a sensation. Its Rahman soundtrack and Aamir's tapori Munna remain beloved 90s nostalgia.
rows: Aamir Khan, Urmila Matondkar, Jackie Shroff, Gulshan Grover
Won 7 Filmfare Awards incl. Best Music (A. R. Rahman)
dyk: A. R. Rahman's first Hindi film with an original score; the album sold about 3.2 million units.

title: Satya
starring: J. D. Chakravarthy, Urmila Matondkar, Manoj Bajpayee, Shefali Shah
honours: National Award for Supporting Actor (Manoj Bajpayee); 6 Filmfare Awards
head: Satya
craze: A gritty, realistic portrait of Mumbai's underworld that birthed the 'Mumbai noir' genre. Manoj Bajpayee's Bhiku Mhatre became legendary and launched a wave of new talent.
rows: J. D. Chakravarthy, Urmila Matondkar, Manoj Bajpayee, Shefali Shah
National Award for Supporting Actor (Manoj Bajpayee); 6 Filmfare Awards
dyk: Written by Anurag Kashyap and Saurabh Shukla; made on a budget of about ₹2.5 crore.

title: Company
starring: Ajay Devgn, Vivek Oberoi, Mohanlal, Manisha Koirala
honours: Won 6 Filmfare Awards incl. Best Male Debut (Vivek Oberoi)
head: Company
craze: A cool, procedural look at a gang empire splitting apart, inspired by real underworld rivalries. Its sleek style and 'Khallas' song made it a defining Hindi gangster film.
rows: Ajay Devgn, Vivek Oberoi, Mohanlal, Manisha Koirala
Won 6 Filmfare Awards incl. Best Male Debut (Vivek Oberoi)
dyk: Mohanlal's Hindi debut; Danny Boyle cited it as an influence on Slumdog Millionaire.

title: Bhoot
starring: Ajay Devgn, Urmila Matondkar, Nana Patekar, Rekha
honours: Filmfare Best Actress (Critics) for Urmila Matondkar
head: Bhoot
craze: A lean, sound-driven haunted-apartment chiller that ditched Bollywood horror cliches. Urmila Matondkar's possessed performance still gives viewers nightmares.
rows: Ajay Devgn, Urmila Matondkar, Nana Patekar, Rekha
Filmfare Best Actress (Critics) for Urmila Matondkar
dyk: Unusual for Bollywood, it plays without songs except one over the end credits.

title: Sarkar
starring: Amitabh Bachchan, Abhishek Bachchan, Kay Kay Menon, Katrina Kaif
honours: Filmfare Best Supporting Actor (Abhishek Bachchan)
head: Sarkar
craze: Amitabh Bachchan's brooding, all-powerful Subhash Nagre became an iconic screen patriarch. Its 'Govinda' chant and intense family politics made it a modern classic.
rows: Amitabh Bachchan, Abhishek Bachchan, Kay Kay Menon, Katrina Kaif
dyk: An unofficial reimagining of The Godfather set in modern-day Mumbai.

title: Sarkar Raj
starring: Amitabh Bachchan, Abhishek Bachchan, Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, Supriya Pathak
honours: Filmfare nom for Best Supporting Actor (Abhishek Bachchan)
head: Sarkar Raj
craze: The sequel expanded Sarkar's world into high-stakes power politics and betrayal. Seeing Amitabh, Abhishek and Aishwarya together drew huge curiosity.
rows: Amitabh Bachchan, Abhishek Bachchan, Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, Supriya Pathak
Filmfare nom for Best Supporting Actor (Abhishek Bachchan)
dyk: It premiered at the 2008 Cannes Film Festival with all three Bachchans in lead roles.

title: Rakta Charitra
starring: Vivek Oberoi, Shatrughan Sinha, Abhimanyu Singh, Radhika Apte
head: Rakta Charitra
craze: A brutal, unflinching saga of factional revenge that later gained cult status. Vivek Oberoi's ferocious turn is often called the best of his career.
rows: Vivek Oberoi, Shatrughan Sinha, Abhimanyu Singh, Radhika Apte
dyk: Shot simultaneously in Telugu and Hindi, based on the life of politician Paritala Ravi.

title: D Company
starring: Ashwath Kanth, Rudra Kanth, Naina Ganguly, Irra Mor
head: D Company
craze: Varma returned to his favorite underworld territory, tracing the birth of a crime syndicate. Fans of his gangster films tuned in for the raw, docudrama-style storytelling.
rows: Ashwath Kanth, Rudra Kanth, Naina Ganguly, Irra Mor
dyk: A prelude to RGV's D Company web series, charting Dawood Ibrahim's rise in Mumbai.

title: Ugramm
starring: Sriimurali, Haripriya, Tilak Shekar, Atul Kulkarni
honours: SIIMA Best Debut Director (Prashanth Neel)
head: Ugramm
craze: A gritty, stylish actioner that revived Sriimurali's career and announced Neel's dark visual signature. Fans now revisit it as the blueprint for Salaar.
rows: Sriimurali, Haripriya, Tilak Shekar, Atul Kulkarni
dyk: Neel's debut; its story was later retold on a bigger scale as Salaar: Part 1 – Ceasefire (2023).

title: K.G.F: Chapter 1
starring: Yash, Srinidhi Shetty, Ramachandra Raju, Anant Nag
honours: 2 National Awards (Action, Special Effects); Filmfare South Best Film
head: K.G.F: Chapter 1
craze: Rocky's rise from Bombay's streets to the gold fields made Yash a pan-India star. Its swaggering dialogues and mythic hero worship put Kannada cinema on the national map.
rows: Yash, Srinidhi Shetty, Ramachandra Raju, Anant Nag
2 National Awards (Action, Special Effects); Filmfare South Best Film
dyk: The first Kannada film to gross ₹100 crore and then ₹200 crore worldwide.

title: K.G.F: Chapter 2
starring: Yash, Sanjay Dutt, Raveena Tandon, Srinidhi Shetty
honours: National Award for Best Kannada Film
head: K.G.F: Chapter 2
craze: A thunderous, larger-than-life sequel that turned theaters into stadiums across India. Lines like 'Violence, violence, violence' became instant mass anthems.
rows: Yash, Sanjay Dutt, Raveena Tandon, Srinidhi Shetty
National Award for Best Kannada Film
dyk: The highest-grossing Kannada film ever and the first Kannada film released in IMAX.

title: Salaar: Part 1
starring: Prabhas, Prithviraj Sukumaran, Shruti Haasan, Jagapathi Babu
head: Salaar: Part 1
craze: A towering friendship-turned-feud story set in the fictional city-state of Khansaar, built on huge mass-hero moments. Fans embraced Prabhas's brooding comeback and the dense world-building that sets up a full saga.
rows: Prabhas, Prithviraj Sukumaran, Shruti Haasan, Jagapathi Babu
dyk: Grossed over ₹700 crore worldwide, one of the biggest Indian hits of 2023.

title: Jigarthanda
starring: Siddharth, Bobby Simha, Lakshmi Menon, Karunakaran
honours: Won 2 National Film Awards incl. Best Supporting Actor (Bobby Simha)
head: Jigarthanda
craze: A wannabe filmmaker studies a feared Madurai gangster, and the tables turn in wildly funny ways. It became a cult favourite for its meta take on cinema itself and spawned a 2023 spiritual sequel.
rows: Siddharth, Bobby Simha, Lakshmi Menon, Karunakaran
Won 2 National Film Awards incl. Best Supporting Actor (Bobby Simha)
dyk: Bobby Simha won the National Award for playing the gangster Assault Sethu.

title: Mahaan
starring: Vikram, Dhruv Vikram, Simran, Bobby Simha
head: Mahaan
craze: A schoolteacher raised on strict Gandhian ideals breaks free and builds a liquor empire, only to clash with his own son. Fans relish the father-son showdown and Vikram's swaggering, emotional lead turn.
rows: Vikram, Dhruv Vikram, Simran, Bobby Simha
dyk: Real-life father and son Vikram and Dhruv Vikram face off on screen; it premiered on Prime Video.

title: Memories of Murder
starring: Song Kang-ho, Kim Sang-kyung, Kim Roe-ha, Park Hae-il
honours: Won Grand Bell Award for Best Film
head: Memories of Murder
craze: Bumbling rural cops and a city detective chase a killer they cannot catch, mixing dark humour with dread. Its haunting final stare into the camera made it one of the most celebrated Korean films ever.
rows: Song Kang-ho, Kim Sang-kyung, Kim Roe-ha, Park Hae-il
Won Grand Bell Award for Best Film
dyk: Based on Korea's Hwaseong serial murders; the real killer was identified in 2019, 16 years after release.

title: Mother
starring: Kim Hye-ja, Won Bin, Jin Goo, Yoon Je-moon
honours: Premiered in Un Certain Regard at Cannes 2009
head: Mother
craze: A widow turns detective to clear her intellectually disabled son of murder, and her devotion slides into something darker. Viewers revere its twisty plot and Kim Hye-ja's unforgettable central performance.
rows: Kim Hye-ja, Won Bin, Jin Goo, Yoon Je-moon
Premiered in Un Certain Regard at Cannes 2009
dyk: Kim Hye-ja, famed for TV mother roles, subverted her image as an obsessive, fierce parent.

title: Snowpiercer
starring: Chris Evans, Song Kang-ho, Tilda Swinton, Jamie Bell
head: Snowpiercer
craze: The last humans ride a perpetual train where class is set by carriage, and the poor storm forward car by car. Its blunt, inventive allegory of inequality made it a cult favourite and a gateway to Bong's work.
rows: Chris Evans, Song Kang-ho, Tilda Swinton, Jamie Bell
dyk: Adapted from the French graphic novel Le Transperceneige; later spun off into a TV series.

title: Parasite
starring: Song Kang-ho, Lee Sun-kyun, Cho Yeo-jeong, Choi Woo-shik
honours: Won 4 Oscars incl. Best Picture; Palme d'Or
head: Parasite
craze: A poor family cons its way into a wealthy household until a hidden secret upends everything. Its razor-sharp take on class broke the subtitle barrier for global audiences and became a worldwide phenomenon.
rows: Song Kang-ho, Lee Sun-kyun, Cho Yeo-jeong, Choi Woo-shik
Won 4 Oscars incl. Best Picture; Palme d'Or
dyk: First non-English-language film to win the Oscar for Best Picture.

title: 12 Angry Men
starring: Henry Fonda, Lee J. Cobb, Ed Begley, E. G. Marshall
honours: 3 Oscar noms incl. Best Picture; Golden Bear
head: 12 Angry Men
craze: One juror's doubt slowly turns a room of eleven certain men in a murder trial. It is a masterclass in tension from pure dialogue and remains a staple of classrooms, law schools and remakes worldwide.
rows: Henry Fonda, Lee J. Cobb, Ed Begley, E. G. Marshall
3 Oscar noms incl. Best Picture; Golden Bear
dyk: Almost the entire film unfolds inside a single jury room.

title: Dog Day Afternoon
starring: Al Pacino, John Cazale, Charles Durning, Chris Sarandon
honours: Won Oscar for Best Original Screenplay (6 noms)
head: Dog Day Afternoon
craze: A botched bank heist turns into a media circus on a sweltering New York day. Pacino's electric 'Attica!' moment and the film's raw humanity made it a defining work of 1970s American cinema.
rows: Al Pacino, John Cazale, Charles Durning, Chris Sarandon
Won Oscar for Best Original Screenplay (6 noms)
dyk: Based on John Wojtowicz's real 1972 Brooklyn bank robbery.

title: Network
starring: Faye Dunaway, William Holden, Peter Finch, Robert Duvall
honours: Won 4 Oscars incl. Best Actor and Best Actress (10 noms)
head: Network
craze: A news anchor's on-air breakdown becomes a ratings goldmine for a ruthless network. Its 'mad as hell' rant and eerily accurate vision of outrage-driven media feel more prophetic with every decade.
rows: Faye Dunaway, William Holden, Peter Finch, Robert Duvall
Won 4 Oscars incl. Best Actor and Best Actress (10 noms)
dyk: Peter Finch became the first posthumous winner of an acting Oscar.

title: Akira
starring: Mitsuo Iwata, Nozomu Sasaki, Mami Koyama, Taro Ishida
head: Akira
craze: Biker gangs, psychic powers and government secrets collide in a ruined Neo-Tokyo. It introduced many Western viewers to anime and its imagery, like Kaneda's bike slide, is endlessly referenced.
rows: Mitsuo Iwata, Nozomu Sasaki, Mami Koyama, Taro Ishida
dyk: Its roughly ¥1.1 billion budget made it the most expensive anime film of its time.

title: Rashomon
starring: Toshiro Mifune, Machiko Kyō, Masayuki Mori, Takashi Shimura
honours: Golden Lion at Venice; Honorary Academy Award
head: Rashomon
craze: A crime in a forest is told four ways by four witnesses, none fully trustworthy. It opened Japanese cinema to the world and its unreliable-narrator structure is still copied everywhere.
rows: Toshiro Mifune, Machiko Kyō, Masayuki Mori, Takashi Shimura
Golden Lion at Venice; Honorary Academy Award
dyk: Gave its name to the 'Rashomon effect' of contradictory eyewitness accounts.

title: Ikiru
starring: Takashi Shimura, Shin'ichi Himori, Haruo Tanaka, Minoru Chiaki
honours: Kinema Junpo Best Film of 1952
head: Ikiru
craze: A dying bureaucrat searches for meaning and finds it in building a small park. Its quiet, devastating humanity, and the image of Shimura on the swing in the snow, moves viewers in every generation.
rows: Takashi Shimura, Shin'ichi Himori, Haruo Tanaka, Minoru Chiaki
dyk: Remade in 2022 as Living, with Bill Nighy and a script by Kazuo Ishiguro.

title: Seven Samurai
starring: Toshiro Mifune, Takashi Shimura, Keiko Tsushima, Yoshio Inaba
honours: Silver Lion at Venice; 2 Oscar noms
head: Seven Samurai
craze: Villagers hire a ragtag band of ronin to defend them against bandits. It essentially invented the 'assemble the team' blueprint that action films still follow and is regularly ranked among the greatest films ever.
rows: Toshiro Mifune, Takashi Shimura, Keiko Tsushima, Yoshio Inaba
Silver Lion at Venice; 2 Oscar noms
dyk: Remade in Hollywood as The Magnificent Seven (1960).

title: Throne of Blood
starring: Toshiro Mifune, Isuzu Yamada, Takashi Shimura, Minoru Chiaki
head: Throne of Blood
craze: Shakespeare's Macbeth is reimagined in feudal Japan, with fog, Noh theatre and ghostly prophecy. Many consider it the finest screen Macbeth, and Mifune's arrow-riddled death is legendary.
rows: Toshiro Mifune, Isuzu Yamada, Takashi Shimura, Minoru Chiaki
dyk: For the finale, real arrows were shot by archers toward Toshiro Mifune.

title: The Hidden Fortress
starring: Toshiro Mifune, Misa Uehara, Minoru Chiaki, Kamatari Fujiwara
honours: Silver Bear for Best Director at Berlin
head: The Hidden Fortress
craze: A general escorts a princess and her gold through enemy territory with two greedy peasants in tow. Its playful mix of adventure and comedy made it Kurosawa's biggest hit at the time and a seed of Star Wars.
rows: Toshiro Mifune, Misa Uehara, Minoru Chiaki, Kamatari Fujiwara
Silver Bear for Best Director at Berlin
dyk: George Lucas cited its two bickering peasants as an inspiration for Star Wars' R2-D2 and C-3PO.

title: Yojimbo
starring: Toshiro Mifune, Tatsuya Nakadai, Yoko Tsukasa, Isuzu Yamada
honours: Volpi Cup Best Actor (Mifune) at Venice; Oscar nom
head: Yojimbo
craze: A wandering ronin plays two warring gangs against each other in a dusty town. Mifune's shrugging, cynical antihero became the template for the spaghetti western's Man with No Name.
rows: Toshiro Mifune, Tatsuya Nakadai, Yoko Tsukasa, Isuzu Yamada
Volpi Cup Best Actor (Mifune) at Venice; Oscar nom
dyk: Unofficially remade by Sergio Leone as A Fistful of Dollars (1964).

title: Sanjuro
starring: Toshiro Mifune, Tatsuya Nakadai, Yūzō Kayama, Takashi Shimura
head: Sanjuro
craze: Mifune's scruffy ronin returns to mentor nine earnest young samurai through a political plot. Lighter and funnier than Yojimbo, it is adored for its wit and that lightning-fast closing duel.
rows: Toshiro Mifune, Tatsuya Nakadai, Yūzō Kayama, Takashi Shimura
dyk: Its final duel ends in a shocking geyser of blood that changed screen sword fights.

title: High and Low
starring: Toshiro Mifune, Tatsuya Nakadai, Kyōko Kagawa, Tsutomu Yamazaki
head: High and Low
craze: An executive must decide whether to pay a ransom for his chauffeur's kidnapped son. It splits into a gripping moral drama and a meticulous police procedural, and inspired Spike Lee's 2025 remake.
rows: Toshiro Mifune, Tatsuya Nakadai, Kyōko Kagawa, Tsutomu Yamazaki
dyk: Shot in black and white, it uses a single burst of pink smoke as a key clue.

title: Kagemusha
starring: Tatsuya Nakadai, Tsutomu Yamazaki, Kenichi Hagiwara
honours: Palme d'Or; 2 Oscar noms
head: Kagemusha
craze: A petty thief is made to impersonate a dead warlord to keep his clan together. Its vivid colours and vast battle images marked Kurosawa's triumphant late-career return.
rows: Tatsuya Nakadai, Tsutomu Yamazaki, Kenichi Hagiwara
dyk: George Lucas and Francis Ford Coppola helped secure its international funding.

title: Ran
starring: Tatsuya Nakadai, Akira Terao, Jinpachi Nezu, Mieko Harada
honours: Won Oscar for Best Costume Design (4 noms incl. Best Director)
head: Ran
craze: An aging warlord divides his realm among three sons and descends into chaos and madness. Its colour-coded armies and burning-castle sequence are among the most staggering spectacles ever filmed.
rows: Tatsuya Nakadai, Akira Terao, Jinpachi Nezu, Mieko Harada
Won Oscar for Best Costume Design (4 noms incl. Best Director)
dyk: A King Lear retelling; it was the most expensive Japanese film ever made at the time.

title: The Terminator
starring: Arnold Schwarzenegger, Michael Biehn, Linda Hamilton, Paul Winfield
honours: Selected for the US National Film Registry
head: The Terminator
craze: A relentless cyborg is sent back in time to kill the mother of humanity's future savior. It made Schwarzenegger a star, coined 'I'll be back' and launched one of sci-fi's biggest franchises.
rows: Arnold Schwarzenegger, Michael Biehn, Linda Hamilton, Paul Winfield
Selected for the US National Film Registry
dyk: Made for about $6.4 million, it earned over ten times its budget.

title: Aliens
starring: Sigourney Weaver, Michael Biehn, Paul Reiser, Lance Henriksen
honours: Won 2 Oscars (7 noms incl. Best Actress for Weaver)
head: Aliens
craze: Ripley returns with a squad of marines to face an entire hive of xenomorphs. It turned horror into pulse-pounding action and gave cinema one of its most iconic heroines.
rows: Sigourney Weaver, Michael Biehn, Paul Reiser, Lance Henriksen
Won 2 Oscars (7 noms incl. Best Actress for Weaver)
dyk: Sigourney Weaver earned a rare Best Actress Oscar nomination for a sci-fi action role.

title: The Abyss
starring: Ed Harris, Mary Elizabeth Mastrantonio, Michael Biehn, Todd Graff
honours: Won Oscar for Best Visual Effects (4 noms)
head: The Abyss
craze: Deep-sea oil workers encounter something otherworldly during a tense rescue mission. Its water tentacle pioneered CGI that led straight to T2, and fans prize its emotional underwater drama.
rows: Ed Harris, Mary Elizabeth Mastrantonio, Michael Biehn, Todd Graff
Won Oscar for Best Visual Effects (4 noms)
dyk: Shot largely in a flooded, unfinished nuclear power plant reactor vessel.

title: Terminator 2: Judgment Day
starring: Arnold Schwarzenegger, Linda Hamilton, Edward Furlong, Robert Patrick
honours: Won 4 Oscars incl. Best Visual Effects
head: Terminator 2: Judgment Day
craze: The Terminator returns as a protector against a shape-shifting new killer. It set the gold standard for action sequels and blockbuster effects, and Linda Hamilton's Sarah Connor redefined the action heroine.
rows: Arnold Schwarzenegger, Linda Hamilton, Edward Furlong, Robert Patrick
Won 4 Oscars incl. Best Visual Effects
dyk: Its liquid-metal T-1000 was a landmark in computer-generated effects.

title: True Lies
starring: Arnold Schwarzenegger, Jamie Lee Curtis, Tom Arnold, Bill Paxton
honours: Golden Globe for Jamie Lee Curtis; Oscar nom for VFX
head: True Lies
craze: A secret agent hides his double life from his wife until a terror plot drags her in. Its mix of huge stunts, marital comedy and a Harrier-jet finale made it a crowd-pleasing 90s favourite.
rows: Arnold Schwarzenegger, Jamie Lee Curtis, Tom Arnold, Bill Paxton
Golden Globe for Jamie Lee Curtis; Oscar nom for VFX
dyk: Widely cited as the first film with a production budget over $100 million.

title: Titanic
starring: Leonardo DiCaprio, Kate Winslet, Billy Zane, Kathy Bates
honours: Won 11 Oscars incl. Best Picture (14 noms)
head: Titanic
craze: A doomed romance aboard the ill-fated liner captured the world, sending viewers back to theatres again and again. Its songs, lines and bow-of-the-ship pose became pop-culture fixtures.
rows: Leonardo DiCaprio, Kate Winslet, Billy Zane, Kathy Bates
Won 11 Oscars incl. Best Picture (14 noms)
dyk: Its 11 Oscar wins tie the all-time record with Ben-Hur and The Return of the King.

title: Avatar
starring: Sam Worthington, Zoe Saldaña, Stephen Lang, Michelle Rodriguez
honours: Won 3 Oscars (9 noms incl. Best Picture)
head: Avatar
craze: A paralysed marine inhabits an alien body on Pandora and switches sides in a war for its resources. Its immersive 3D and performance-capture world sparked a global 3D boom and an event-cinema franchise.
rows: Sam Worthington, Zoe Saldaña, Stephen Lang, Michelle Rodriguez
Won 3 Oscars (9 noms incl. Best Picture)
dyk: The highest-grossing film of all time worldwide.

title: Avatar: The Way of Water
starring: Sam Worthington, Zoe Saldaña, Sigourney Weaver, Stephen Lang
honours: Won Oscar for Best Visual Effects (4 noms incl. Best Picture)
head: Avatar: The Way of Water
craze: The Sully family flees to Pandora's ocean reefs as old enemies return. Audiences flocked to its breathtaking underwater worlds, proving doubters wrong 13 years after the original.
rows: Sam Worthington, Zoe Saldaña, Sigourney Weaver, Stephen Lang
Won Oscar for Best Visual Effects (4 noms incl. Best Picture)
dyk: Pioneered underwater performance capture; it is the third-highest-grossing film ever.

title: Avatar: Fire and Ash
starring: Sam Worthington, Zoe Saldaña, Sigourney Weaver, Stephen Lang
honours: Won Oscar for Best Visual Effects
head: Avatar: Fire and Ash
craze: The Sullys face the volcanic Ash People led by Varang, revealing a hostile side of the Na'vi. Fans came for its fiery new landscapes and darker tone, pushing it past $1 billion within weeks.
rows: Sam Worthington, Zoe Saldaña, Sigourney Weaver, Stephen Lang
Won Oscar for Best Visual Effects
dyk: Its 197-minute runtime is the longest of the Avatar films so far.

title: Following
starring: Jeremy Theobald, Alex Haw, Lucy Russell, John Nolan
head: Following
craze: A lonely writer who tails strangers falls in with a charismatic burglar. Fans treasure this lean, scrappy debut for showing Nolan's puzzle-box storytelling in its rawest form.
rows: Jeremy Theobald, Alex Haw, Lucy Russell, John Nolan
dyk: Shot on weekends in black and white for a reported budget of about $6,000.

title: Memento
starring: Guy Pearce, Carrie-Anne Moss, Joe Pantoliano
honours: 2 Oscar noms incl. Best Original Screenplay
head: Memento
craze: A man with no short-term memory hunts his wife's killer using tattoos and Polaroids. Its reverse structure made audiences rewatch and debate it, establishing Nolan as a major new talent.
rows: Guy Pearce, Carrie-Anne Moss, Joe Pantoliano
2 Oscar noms incl. Best Original Screenplay
dyk: Colour scenes run backwards while black-and-white scenes run forwards until they meet.

title: Insomnia
starring: Al Pacino, Robin Williams, Hilary Swank, Maura Tierney
head: Insomnia
craze: A sleepless LA detective investigates a murder in Alaska's endless daylight while hiding his own mistake. Fans especially praise Robin Williams's chilling against-type turn as the killer.
rows: Al Pacino, Robin Williams, Hilary Swank, Maura Tierney
dyk: A remake of a 1997 Norwegian film and Nolan's only feature he didn't write.

title: Batman Begins
starring: Christian Bale, Michael Caine, Liam Neeson, Katie Holmes
honours: Oscar nom for Best Cinematography
head: Batman Begins
craze: Bruce Wayne turns fear into a weapon as he becomes Gotham's protector. Its realistic tone rebooted Batman and changed how studios approached superhero films.
rows: Christian Bale, Michael Caine, Liam Neeson, Katie Holmes
dyk: Rebooted Batman eight years after Batman & Robin with a grounded origin story.

title: The Prestige
starring: Hugh Jackman, Christian Bale, Scarlett Johansson, Michael Caine
honours: 2 Oscar noms (Art Direction, Cinematography)
head: The Prestige
craze: Two rival Victorian magicians sacrifice everything to outdo each other's ultimate trick. Its layered twists reward repeat viewing, and fans rank it among Nolan's most underrated films.
rows: Hugh Jackman, Christian Bale, Scarlett Johansson, Michael Caine
dyk: David Bowie plays the real-life inventor Nikola Tesla.

title: The Dark Knight
starring: Christian Bale, Heath Ledger, Aaron Eckhart, Gary Oldman
honours: Won 2 Oscars incl. posthumous Best Supporting Actor (Ledger)
head: The Dark Knight
craze: Batman faces the Joker, an agent of chaos who tests Gotham's soul. Heath Ledger's Joker and the film's crime-epic ambitions made it the benchmark every superhero movie is measured against.
rows: Christian Bale, Heath Ledger, Aaron Eckhart, Gary Oldman
Won 2 Oscars incl. posthumous Best Supporting Actor (Ledger)
dyk: Its Best Picture snub helped push the Academy to expand the category beyond five nominees.

title: Inception
starring: Leonardo DiCaprio, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Elliot Page, Tom Hardy
honours: Won 4 Oscars (8 noms incl. Best Picture)
head: Inception
craze: A team of thieves plants an idea inside a target's dreams, layers deep. Its spinning-top ending and Hans Zimmer's booming score sparked endless debates and countless parodies.
rows: Leonardo DiCaprio, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Elliot Page, Tom Hardy
Won 4 Oscars (8 noms incl. Best Picture)
dyk: The rotating hallway fight was shot in a real spinning set, not CGI.

title: The Dark Knight Rises
starring: Christian Bale, Tom Hardy, Anne Hathaway, Gary Oldman
head: The Dark Knight Rises
craze: Eight years later, a broken Batman returns to face the masked revolutionary Bane. It closed the trilogy on an epic scale, and Bane's voice and lines became instant meme material.
rows: Christian Bale, Tom Hardy, Anne Hathaway, Gary Oldman
dyk: Its opening plane hijack was shot in IMAX with a real aircraft over Scotland.

title: Interstellar
starring: Matthew McConaughey, Anne Hathaway, Jessica Chastain, Michael Caine
honours: Won Oscar for Best Visual Effects (5 noms)
head: Interstellar
craze: Astronauts journey through a wormhole to find humanity a new home while time slips away from those left behind. Its father-daughter heart and organ-driven score keep drawing huge crowds to re-releases.
rows: Matthew McConaughey, Anne Hathaway, Jessica Chastain, Michael Caine
Won Oscar for Best Visual Effects (5 noms)
dyk: Its black hole render, built with physicist Kip Thorne, led to published scientific papers.

title: Dunkirk
starring: Fionn Whitehead, Tom Hardy, Mark Rylance, Kenneth Branagh
honours: Won 3 Oscars (8 noms incl. Best Picture)
head: Dunkirk
craze: The 1940 evacuation is told on land, sea and air with almost no backstory and constant tension. Its ticking-clock score and immersive IMAX visuals made it a visceral theatrical experience.
rows: Fionn Whitehead, Tom Hardy, Mark Rylance, Kenneth Branagh
Won 3 Oscars (8 noms incl. Best Picture)
dyk: Told across three interlocking timelines: one week, one day and one hour.

title: Tenet
starring: John David Washington, Robert Pattinson, Elizabeth Debicki, Kenneth Branagh
honours: Won Oscar for Best Visual Effects (2 noms)
head: Tenet
craze: A secret agent learns to manipulate time inversion to stop a global catastrophe. Released in the pandemic, it became the film fans love to decode, with its palindromic plot fuelling endless explainers.
rows: John David Washington, Robert Pattinson, Elizabeth Debicki, Kenneth Branagh
Won Oscar for Best Visual Effects (2 noms)
dyk: Nolan crashed a real Boeing 747 into a hangar rather than using CGI.

title: Oppenheimer
starring: Cillian Murphy, Emily Blunt, Matt Damon, Robert Downey Jr.
honours: Won 7 Oscars incl. Best Picture (13 noms)
head: Oppenheimer
craze: The story of the man who led the atomic bomb project and wrestled with its consequences. Paired with Barbie as 'Barbenheimer', it turned a three-hour historical drama into a global event.
rows: Cillian Murphy, Emily Blunt, Matt Damon, Robert Downey Jr.
Won 7 Oscars incl. Best Picture (13 noms)
dyk: The Trinity test explosion was recreated with practical effects rather than CGI.

title: The Godfather
starring: Marlon Brando, Al Pacino, James Caan, Robert Duvall
honours: Won 3 Oscars incl. Best Picture and Best Actor
head: The Godfather
craze: The Corleone family saga traces Michael's transformation from outsider to ruthless don. Its lines, score and imagery became the definitive picture of the mafia and it is routinely named the greatest film ever.
rows: Marlon Brando, Al Pacino, James Caan, Robert Duvall
Won 3 Oscars incl. Best Picture and Best Actor
dyk: Marlon Brando declined his Best Actor Oscar, sending Sacheen Littlefeather in his place.

title: The Godfather Part II
starring: Al Pacino, Robert De Niro, Robert Duvall, Diane Keaton
honours: Won 6 Oscars incl. Best Picture (11 noms)
head: The Godfather Part II
craze: Michael's tightening grip on power is intercut with young Vito's rise in early 1900s New York. Many fans argue it surpasses the original, and De Niro won an Oscar playing the role Brando made famous.
rows: Al Pacino, Robert De Niro, Robert Duvall, Diane Keaton
Won 6 Oscars incl. Best Picture (11 noms)
dyk: The first sequel to win the Oscar for Best Picture.

title: Pulp Fiction
starring: John Travolta, Samuel L. Jackson, Uma Thurman, Bruce Willis
honours: Palme d'Or; Won Oscar for Best Original Screenplay (7 noms)
head: Pulp Fiction
craze: Intertwined LA crime stories told out of order, packed with pop-culture chatter and sudden violence. It revived Travolta's career, reshaped 90s indie film and its dance scene and quotes are endlessly recreated.
rows: John Travolta, Samuel L. Jackson, Uma Thurman, Bruce Willis
Palme d'Or; Won Oscar for Best Original Screenplay (7 noms)
dyk: Made for about $8.5 million, it became the first indie film to pass $100 million in the US.

title: Heat
starring: Al Pacino, Robert De Niro, Val Kilmer, Jon Voight
head: Heat
craze: A driven LA detective and a disciplined master thief circle each other in a battle of equals. Its downtown shootout is studied by filmmakers and even cited in tactical training, making it a crime-film touchstone.
rows: Al Pacino, Robert De Niro, Val Kilmer, Jon Voight
dyk: Its diner scene was the first time Pacino and De Niro shared the screen face to face.

title: City of God
starring: Alexandre Rodrigues, Leandro Firmino, Phellipe Haagensen, Seu Jorge
honours: 4 Oscar noms incl. Best Director
head: City of God
craze: A budding photographer chronicles decades of gang war in a Rio housing project. Its kinetic style and raw energy made it a global sensation and a landmark of Brazilian cinema.
rows: Alexandre Rodrigues, Leandro Firmino, Phellipe Haagensen, Seu Jorge
dyk: Most of the cast were non-professionals recruited from Rio's favelas.

title: Oldboy
starring: Choi Min-sik, Yoo Ji-tae, Kang Hye-jung
honours: Grand Prix at Cannes 2004
head: Oldboy
craze: A man imprisoned for 15 years without explanation is freed and given five days to find out why. Its shocking twist and brutal one-take fight made it a cult classic and put Korean cinema on the global map.
rows: Choi Min-sik, Yoo Ji-tae, Kang Hye-jung
dyk: The corridor hammer fight was filmed as a single continuous side-scrolling take.

title: No Country for Old Men
starring: Tommy Lee Jones, Javier Bardem, Josh Brolin, Woody Harrelson
honours: Won 4 Oscars incl. Best Picture
head: No Country for Old Men
craze: A hunter takes drug money from a desert shootout and is stalked by the relentless killer Anton Chigurh. Bardem's coin-toss villain and the film's bleak, unresolved ending keep audiences talking.
rows: Tommy Lee Jones, Javier Bardem, Josh Brolin, Woody Harrelson
dyk: Has almost no musical score, relying on silence and natural sound for tension.

title: There Will Be Blood
starring: Daniel Day-Lewis, Paul Dano, Kevin J. O'Connor, Ciarán Hinds
honours: Won 2 Oscars incl. Best Actor (Day-Lewis) (8 noms)
head: There Will Be Blood
craze: A ruthless oilman's greed collides with a fiery young preacher in early-1900s California. Day-Lewis's towering performance and the 'milkshake' line made it one of the most celebrated films of the century.
rows: Daniel Day-Lewis, Paul Dano, Kevin J. O'Connor, Ciarán Hinds
Won 2 Oscars incl. Best Actor (Day-Lewis) (8 noms)
dyk: Loosely adapted from Upton Sinclair's 1927 novel Oil!

title: Thriller
starring: Epic
box: ~70M copies worldwide; best-selling album ever; 34× Platinum (US)
head: Thriller
craze: Thriller turned the music video into an event and pushed MTV to play Black artists, rewriting pop's rules overnight. Its singles, dance moves and that zombie short film made Jackson the most famous entertainer on the planet.
rows: Billie Jean, Beat It, Thriller, Wanna Be Startin' Somethin'
~70M copies worldwide; best-selling album ever; 34× Platinum (US)
dyk: Seven of its nine tracks became US Top 10 singles; it won a record eight Grammys in one night.

title: Bad
starring: Epic
head: Bad
craze: Following the biggest album of all time, Bad proved Jackson could still dominate, with a tougher sound and a sharper image. The Smooth Criminal lean and the record-breaking Bad world tour cemented him as a global spectacle.
rows: Bad, Smooth Criminal, The Way You Make Me Feel, Man in the Mirror
dyk: First album ever to send five consecutive singles to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.

title: Dangerous
starring: Epic
runtime: Michael Jackson, Teddy Riley, Bill Bottrell, Bruce Swedien
head: Dangerous
craze: By teaming with Teddy Riley, Jackson pulled new jack swing and hip-hop grit into his pop, keeping him current in the '90s. Its globe-spanning videos and the Super Bowl XXVII halftime show turned the album into a worldwide event.
rows: Michael Jackson, Teddy Riley, Bill Bottrell, Bruce Swedien
Black or White, Remember the Time, Jam, Heal the World
dyk: The 'Black or White' video premiered simultaneously in 27 countries to a reported 500 million viewers.

title: HIStory: Past, Present and Future, Book I
starring: Epic
runtime: Michael Jackson, Jimmy Jam & Terry Lewis, David Foster, R. Kelly
box: ~20M copies (40M units as a double album); best-selling multi-disc album by a solo artist
head: HIStory: Past, Present and Future, Book I
craze: Half greatest-hits, half defiant new material, HIStory channeled Jackson's anger at the media into his most confrontational songs. 'Earth Song' and 'They Don't Care About Us' became protest anthems far beyond the pop charts.
rows: Michael Jackson, Jimmy Jam & Terry Lewis, David Foster, R. Kelly
Scream, You Are Not Alone, Earth Song, They Don't Care About Us
~20M copies (40M units as a double album); best-selling multi-disc album by a solo artist
dyk: 'You Are Not Alone' was the first song ever to debut at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.

title: Off the Wall
starring: Epic
head: Off the Wall
craze: Off the Wall announced Jackson as an adult solo star and fused disco, funk and soul into a glossy, joyous sound. It began his partnership with Quincy Jones and laid the blueprint for the pop domination that followed.
rows: Don't Stop 'Til You Get Enough, Rock with You, Off the Wall, She's Out of My Life
dyk: First solo album to produce four US Top 10 singles.

title: Back in Black
starring: Atlantic (Albert Productions in Australia)
box: ~50M copies worldwide; best-selling hard rock album ever; Diamond (US)
head: Back in Black
craze: Rebounding from tragedy with new singer Brian Johnson, AC/DC made a record so tight and loud it became the gold standard for hard rock. Its riffs live on in stadiums, films and sports arenas decades later.
rows: Back in Black, You Shook Me All Night Long, Hells Bells, Shoot to Thrill
~50M copies worldwide; best-selling hard rock album ever; Diamond (US)
dyk: Recorded months after Bon Scott's death; the all-black cover was a mark of mourning.

title: Highway to Hell
starring: Atlantic
head: Highway to Hell
craze: Working with Mutt Lange for the first time, AC/DC sharpened their bar-band attack into radio-ready muscle and broke through in America. The title track became one of rock's most defiant road anthems.
rows: Highway to Hell, Touch Too Much, Girls Got Rhythm, If You Want Blood (You've Got It)
dyk: Bon Scott's final album; he died in February 1980, about six months after its release.

title: The Razors Edge
starring: Atco
head: The Razors Edge
craze: After a patchy decade, The Razors Edge revived AC/DC as a commercial force. 'Thunderstruck' and its chanting intro became a stadium and sports-arena staple for a whole new generation.
rows: Thunderstruck, Moneytalks, Are You Ready, Fire Your Guns
dyk: 'Moneytalks' became AC/DC's highest-charting US single, reaching No. 23 on the Hot 100.

title: Let There Be Rock
starring: Albert Productions / Atlantic
head: Let There Be Rock
craze: Raw and relentless, it captured the band's ferocious live energy in the studio and built their reputation as rock's hardest-working road warriors. 'Whole Lotta Rosie' became a concert centrepiece for decades.
rows: Let There Be Rock, Whole Lotta Rosie, Bad Boy Boogie, Hell Ain't a Bad Place to Be
dyk: The first AC/DC album to feature the band's now-iconic lightning-bolt logo.

title: For Those About to Rock We Salute You
starring: Atlantic
head: For Those About to Rock We Salute You
craze: Riding the momentum of Back in Black, it gave AC/DC their first US chart-topper. The cannon-firing title track became the band's traditional show closer and a salute fans still roar back.
rows: For Those About to Rock (We Salute You), Put the Finger on You, Let's Get It Up, Evil Walks
dyk: AC/DC's first album to reach No. 1 on the Billboard 200.

title: Powerage
starring: Atlantic
head: Powerage
craze: Often overlooked by casual fans, Powerage is a musicians' favourite for its bluesy grooves and Bon Scott's street-level storytelling. It shows the band's songwriting depth beneath the volume.
rows: Rock 'n' Roll Damnation, Down Payment Blues, Sin City, Riff Raff
dyk: The first AC/DC album to feature bassist Cliff Williams.

title: High Voltage
starring: Atlantic
head: High Voltage
craze: This was the world's introduction to AC/DC's swaggering, no-frills rock and Bon Scott's cheeky persona. 'It's a Long Way to the Top' with its bagpipes became an unlikely Australian rock anthem.
rows: It's a Long Way to the Top (If You Wanna Rock 'n' Roll), T.N.T., The Jack, High Voltage
dyk: The international debut was compiled from two Australian albums, High Voltage and T.N.T.

title: Black Ice
starring: Columbia
box: No. 1 in 29 countries; 2× Platinum (US); 6M shipped worldwide in 2008
head: Black Ice
craze: Arriving after an eight-year gap, Black Ice proved AC/DC could still outsell nearly everyone, even without downloads. It launched a massive world tour that introduced the band to younger fans.
rows: Rock 'n' Roll Train, Big Jack, Anything Goes, Money Made
No. 1 in 29 countries; 2× Platinum (US); 6M shipped worldwide in 2008
dyk: Topped the charts in 29 countries and was 2008's second-best-selling album worldwide.

title: Appetite for Destruction
starring: Geffen
box: ~30M copies worldwide; 18× Platinum (US); best-selling US debut album
head: Appetite for Destruction
craze: Appetite brought danger and street grit back to a polished hair-metal scene, making Guns N' Roses the most notorious band on earth. 'Sweet Child o' Mine' and its riff became instantly recognisable worldwide.
rows: Welcome to the Jungle, Sweet Child o' Mine, Paradise City, Nightrain
~30M copies worldwide; 18× Platinum (US); best-selling US debut album
dyk: It took nearly a year after release to reach No. 1 on the Billboard 200.

title: Use Your Illusion I
starring: Geffen
head: Use Your Illusion I
craze: The twin-album release was a huge statement of ambition, and fans queued at midnight to buy both. 'November Rain' and its epic wedding video became one of MTV's most-requested clips.
rows: November Rain, Don't Cry, Live and Let Die, Coma
dyk: Released the same day as Use Your Illusion II; the pair debuted at No. 2 and No. 1 in the US.

title: Metallica (The Black Album)
starring: Elektra
runtime: Bob Rock, James Hetfield, Lars Ulrich
head: Metallica (The Black Album)
craze: Slower, heavier and leaner than their thrash work, the Black Album carried metal into the mainstream. 'Enter Sandman' became a global anthem and 'Nothing Else Matters' showed metal could be tender too.
rows: Bob Rock, James Hetfield, Lars Ulrich
Enter Sandman, Nothing Else Matters, The Unforgiven, Sad but True
dyk: Debuted at No. 1 in the US and became one of the best-selling albums of the SoundScan era.

title: Master of Puppets
starring: Elektra
head: Master of Puppets
craze: Widely seen as thrash metal's high point, it became a gold standard for the genre without radio support. Its title track enjoyed a huge new wave of popularity after appearing in Stranger Things in 2022.
rows: Master of Puppets, Battery, Welcome Home (Sanitarium), Orion
dyk: The first metal album added to the US Library of Congress National Recording Registry (2016).

title: Led Zeppelin IV
starring: Atlantic
head: Led Zeppelin IV
craze: It blended folk, blues and heavy rock into one of the most influential albums ever made. 'Stairway to Heaven' became the defining rock epic, played endlessly on FM radio despite never being released as a US single.
rows: Stairway to Heaven, Black Dog, Rock and Roll, When the Levee Breaks
dyk: Officially untitled: the cover shows no band name or title, only four mystic symbols.

title: Paranoid
starring: Vertigo
head: Paranoid
craze: Paranoid essentially defined what heavy metal would sound like: sludgy riffs, dark themes and doom-laden atmosphere. 'Iron Man' and 'War Pigs' became templates copied by generations of metal bands.
rows: Paranoid, Iron Man, War Pigs, Planet Caravan
dyk: The title track was reportedly written in minutes as last-minute filler for the album.

title: The Number of the Beast
starring: EMI
head: The Number of the Beast
craze: With Dickinson's operatic vocals and galloping twin guitars, it made Iron Maiden the flagship of British heavy metal. Its satanic imagery stirred protests in the US, which only boosted the band's fame.
rows: Run to the Hills, The Number of the Beast, Hallowed Be Thy Name, Children of the Damned
dyk: Bruce Dickinson's debut with Iron Maiden and the band's first UK No. 1 album.

starring: Warner Bros.
craze: Eddie Van Halen's synth riff on 'Jump' shocked guitar purists but made the band global superstars. It was the last album with David Lee Roth for over two decades, capping the original line-up at its peak.
rows: Jump, Panama, Hot for Teacher, I'll Wait
dyk: 'Jump' became Van Halen's only US No. 1 single; the album stalled at No. 2 behind Thriller.

title: Slippery When Wet
starring: Mercury
head: Slippery When Wet
craze: Bon Jovi blended hard rock with pop hooks and turned arena rock into a singalong phenomenon. 'Livin' on a Prayer' remains one of the most beloved crowd anthems ever recorded.
rows: Livin' on a Prayer, You Give Love a Bad Name, Wanted Dead or Alive, Never Say Goodbye
dyk: Spent eight weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 and produced two Hot 100 No. 1 singles.

title: The Final Countdown
starring: Epic
head: The Final Countdown
craze: Its fanfare-like synth intro made the title track one of the most recognisable songs in the world. The song remains a fixture at sports events and in pop culture, often played with a wink.
rows: The Final Countdown, Carrie, Rock the Night, Cherokee
dyk: The title track reportedly hit No. 1 in 25 countries.

title: Dr. Feelgood
starring: Elektra
head: Dr. Feelgood
craze: Freshly clean and backed by Bob Rock's huge production, the band made their tightest record and hit their commercial peak. 'Kickstart My Heart' became a high-octane anthem for racing and sports.
rows: Dr. Feelgood, Kickstart My Heart, Without You, Don't Go Away Mad (Just Go Away)
dyk: Mötley Crüe's only No. 1 album on the Billboard 200, recorded after the band got sober.

title: Hysteria
starring: Mercury
head: Hysteria
craze: Mutt Lange's layered, polished production made every song sound like a single, and seven of them were released as one. 'Pour Some Sugar on Me' became a strip-club, stadium and karaoke classic.
rows: Pour Some Sugar on Me, Love Bites, Hysteria, Animal
dyk: Drummer Rick Allen played on it using a custom kit after losing his left arm in a 1984 crash.

title: The Dark Side of the Moon
starring: Harvest (UK) / Capitol (US)
head: The Dark Side of the Moon
craze: A seamless meditation on time, money and madness, it became the ultimate headphone album and a hi-fi showcase. Its prism cover is one of the most recognisable images in music.
rows: Money, Time, Us and Them, The Great Gig in the Sky
dyk: Spent over 900 weeks on the Billboard 200, one of the longest runs in chart history.

title: Nevermind
starring: DGC
head: Nevermind
craze: Nevermind dragged underground alternative rock into the mainstream almost overnight and ended the hair-metal era. 'Smells Like Teen Spirit' became the anthem of Generation X and Kurt Cobain its reluctant voice.
rows: Smells Like Teen Spirit, Come as You Are, Lithium, In Bloom
dyk: In January 1992 it knocked Michael Jackson's Dangerous off No. 1 on the Billboard 200.

title: Ten
starring: Epic
head: Ten
craze: Alongside Nevermind, Ten made Seattle the centre of the rock world. Eddie Vedder's intense vocals and the 'Jeremy' video turned Pearl Jam into one of the most important bands of the '90s.
dyk: A slow burner, it took about a year to break into the top 10, eventually peaking at No. 2.

title: Blood Sugar Sex Magik
starring: Warner Bros.
head: Blood Sugar Sex Magik
craze: Rick Rubin stripped the band's funk-punk down to its grooves, making them mainstream stars. 'Under the Bridge' revealed a vulnerable side that broadened their audience far beyond party rock.
rows: Under the Bridge, Give It Away, Suck My Kiss, Breaking the Girl
dyk: Recorded in a Laurel Canyon mansion the band lived in, reputed to be haunted.

title: Californication
starring: Warner Bros.
head: Californication
craze: Californication was a comeback that reinvented the band with melodic, reflective songs. It became their best-selling album and defined late-'90s rock radio.
rows: Scar Tissue, Otherside, Californication, Around the World
dyk: Marked guitarist John Frusciante's return; 'Scar Tissue' won the Grammy for Best Rock Song.

title: The Black Parade
starring: Reprise
head: The Black Parade
craze: The Black Parade became the defining album of the emo era, with theatrical rock-opera ambitions. That single piano G note opening the title track is now a shorthand for a generation's teenage years.
rows: Welcome to the Black Parade, Famous Last Words, I Don't Love You, Teenagers
dyk: A rock opera that follows 'The Patient,' a man dying of cancer, as he faces death.

title: Dookie
starring: Reprise
head: Dookie
craze: Dookie broke punk into the mainstream and launched the '90s pop-punk boom. Its catchy songs about boredom and anxiety made Green Day superstars and inspired countless garage bands.
rows: Basket Case, Longview, When I Come Around, Welcome to Paradise
dyk: Won the 1995 Grammy for Best Alternative Music Performance.

title: American Idiot
starring: Reprise
box: 15M+ copies worldwide; Grammy for Best Rock Album
head: American Idiot
craze: A politically charged punk rock opera, it revived Green Day's career and captured post-9/11 frustration. 'Boulevard of Broken Dreams' became one of the biggest rock hits of the decade.
rows: American Idiot, Boulevard of Broken Dreams, Holiday, Wake Me Up When September Ends
15M+ copies worldwide; Grammy for Best Rock Album
dyk: Adapted into a Tony-winning Broadway musical in 2010.

title: Definitely Maybe
starring: Creation
runtime: Owen Morris, Noel Gallagher, Mark Coyle
head: Definitely Maybe
craze: Definitely Maybe's swagger and optimism helped launch Britpop and made Oasis the voice of working-class Britain. 'Live Forever' offered hope at a time when grunge was all about despair.
rows: Owen Morris, Noel Gallagher, Mark Coyle
Live Forever, Supersonic, Cigarettes & Alcohol, Rock 'n' Roll Star
dyk: At release it was the fastest-selling debut album in UK history.

title: OK Computer
starring: Parlophone (UK) / Capitol (US)
box: Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album; multi-Platinum (US & UK)
head: OK Computer
craze: OK Computer predicted a world of tech alienation and consumer anxiety just as the internet age dawned. It's regularly named among the greatest albums ever and inspired a wave of more experimental rock.
rows: Paranoid Android, Karma Police, No Surprises, Let Down
Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album; multi-Platinum (US & UK)
dyk: Added to the US National Recording Registry in 2015.

title: Hybrid Theory
starring: Warner Bros.
box: ~32M copies worldwide; best-selling debut album of the 21st century
head: Hybrid Theory
craze: Mixing rap, metal and electronics, Hybrid Theory gave angst a polished, universal voice. 'In the End' became one of the defining songs of the 2000s and remains a streaming giant.
rows: In the End, Crawling, One Step Closer, Papercut
~32M copies worldwide; best-selling debut album of the 21st century
dyk: 'Crawling' won the Grammy for Best Hard Rock Performance.

title: Meteora
starring: Warner Bros. / Machine Shop
head: Meteora
craze: Meteora refined Linkin Park's formula and proved their debut was no fluke. 'Numb' became an anthem for misunderstood teens and later reached a new audience through the 'Numb/Encore' mash-up with Jay-Z.
rows: Numb, Faint, Somewhere I Belong, Breaking the Habit
dyk: Debuted at No. 1 in the US with about 810,000 copies sold in its first week.

title: American Beauty / American Psycho
starring: Island / DCD2
runtime: Jake Sinclair, Butch Walker, J.R. Rotem, Omega, SebastiAn
head: American Beauty / American Psycho
craze: The album completed Fall Out Boy's shift from pop-punk to stadium-sized pop rock. 'Centuries' and 'Immortals' (from Big Hero 6) became sports and movie-trailer staples.
rows: Jake Sinclair, Butch Walker, J.R. Rotem, Omega, SebastiAn
dyk: 'Uma Thurman' samples The Munsters theme; 'Centuries' interpolates Suzanne Vega's 'Tom's Diner'.

title: Hot Fuss
starring: Island (US) / Lizard King (UK)
head: Hot Fuss
craze: Hot Fuss brought glittering new wave synths into 2000s indie rock and made Las Vegas cool. 'Mr. Brightside' became a timeless singalong at every club, wedding and festival.
rows: Mr. Brightside, Somebody Told Me, All These Things That I've Done, Smile Like You Mean It
dyk: 'Mr. Brightside' has become the longest-charting song in UK Singles Chart history.

title: The Eminem Show
starring: Aftermath / Shady / Interscope
box: Best-selling album of 2002 in the US; Diamond (US)
head: The Eminem Show
craze: At the height of his fame, Eminem turned the spotlight on his own celebrity, family and controversies. 'Till I Collapse' became one of the most-played workout songs ever, while 'Without Me' was a satirical blockbuster.
rows: Without Me, Cleanin' Out My Closet, Sing for the Moment, 'Till I Collapse
Best-selling album of 2002 in the US; Diamond (US)
dyk: Eminem produced most of the album himself, a first for one of his major releases.

title: Minutes to Midnight
starring: Warner Bros. / Machine Shop
box: Debuted at No. 1 in the US with ~623,000 first-week sales
head: Minutes to Midnight
craze: Linkin Park dropped most of their nu-metal sound for broader alternative rock, a bold shift that split fans but found new ones. 'What I've Done' became a defining track of their later career.
rows: What I've Done, Bleed It Out, Shadow of the Day, Leave Out All the Rest
Debuted at No. 1 in the US with ~623,000 first-week sales
dyk: Lead single 'What I've Done' was featured in the 2007 film Transformers.

title: A Rush of Blood to the Head
starring: Parlophone (UK) / Capitol (US)
box: Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album; multi-Platinum (US & UK)
head: A Rush of Blood to the Head
craze: This album turned Coldplay from promising newcomers into one of the world's biggest bands. 'Clocks' and 'The Scientist' became piano-driven classics heard everywhere from radio to film.
rows: Clocks, The Scientist, In My Place, God Put a Smile upon Your Face
Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album; multi-Platinum (US & UK)
dyk: 'Clocks' won the Grammy for Record of the Year in 2004.

title: Made in the A.M.
starring: Columbia / Syco
runtime: Julian Bunetta, John Ryan, Jesse Shatkin, Afterhrs, Johan Carlsson, Jamie Scott
head: Made in the A.M.
craze: Their first album without Zayn Malik, it served as a heartfelt farewell before an indefinite hiatus. 'History' became an emotional anthem for fans who grew up with the band.
rows: Julian Bunetta, John Ryan, Jesse Shatkin, Afterhrs, Johan Carlsson, Jamie Scott
Drag Me Down, Perfect, History, Infinity
dyk: The band's final album before their hiatus; 'Drag Me Down' hit No. 1 in the UK.

title: Songs of Anarchy: Seasons 1–4
starring: Columbia
runtime: Bob Thiele Jr., Kurt Sutter, Dave Kushner, Matt Hyde, Matt Drenik, Lions
box: Peaked at No. 130 on the Billboard 200
head: Songs of Anarchy: Seasons 1–4
craze: The soundtrack helped make music a central part of the Sons of Anarchy identity. Its gritty covers and Americana tracks turned the house band, The Forest Rangers, into an act fans sought out on their own.
rows: Bob Thiele Jr., Kurt Sutter, Dave Kushner, Matt Hyde, Matt Drenik, Lions
This Life, John the Revelator, Forever Young, Bird on a Wire
Peaked at No. 130 on the Billboard 200
dyk: Opens with 'This Life' by Curtis Stigers & The Forest Rangers, the show's Emmy-nominated theme.

title: Songs of Anarchy: Seasons 5–7
starring: Columbia
head: Songs of Anarchy: Seasons 5–7
craze: Released after the show's final season, it captured the haunting moods that defined its last chapter. The closing song 'Come Join the Murder' became an unforgettable send-off for fans of the series.
rows: Come Join the Murder, Make It Rain, Bohemian Rhapsody, All Along the Watchtower
dyk: 'Come Join the Murder' by The White Buffalo & The Forest Rangers reached No. 93 on the Hot 100.

title: Hotel California
starring: Asylum
head: Hotel California
craze: Hotel California captured the excess and disillusion behind the California dream. Its title track, with that legendary dual guitar solo, remains one of the most-played rock songs ever.
rows: Hotel California, New Kid in Town, Life in the Fast Lane, Wasted Time
dyk: The title track won the Grammy for Record of the Year in 1978.

title: Rumours
starring: Warner Bros.
runtime: Fleetwood Mac, Ken Caillat, Richard Dashut
box: ~40M copies worldwide; 21× Platinum (US); Grammy for Album of the Year
head: Rumours
craze: Rumours turned real heartbreak into polished, irresistible pop rock, and fans loved hearing the drama unfold in the lyrics. It found a new generation when 'Dreams' went viral on TikTok in 2020.
rows: Fleetwood Mac, Ken Caillat, Richard Dashut
Dreams, Go Your Own Way, Don't Stop, The Chain
~40M copies worldwide; 21× Platinum (US); Grammy for Album of the Year
dyk: Written and recorded while both of the band's couples were breaking up.

title: The Joshua Tree
starring: Island
box: ~25M copies worldwide; Grammy for Album of the Year
head: The Joshua Tree
craze: The Joshua Tree made U2 the biggest band in the world, with spacious, soaring songs about America's myths and realities. Its anthems became stadium standards for decades.
rows: With or Without You, I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For, Where the Streets Have No Name, Bullet the Blue Sky
~25M copies worldwide; Grammy for Album of the Year
dyk: U2's first US No. 1 album, producing their first two Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 singles.

title: Born in the U.S.A.
starring: Columbia
runtime: Jon Landau, Chuck Plotkin, Bruce Springsteen, Steven Van Zandt
head: Born in the U.S.A.
craze: This album made Springsteen a global superstar and an icon of working-class America. Its title track, often mistaken for a patriotic anthem, is actually a bitter protest about Vietnam veterans.
rows: Jon Landau, Chuck Plotkin, Bruce Springsteen, Steven Van Zandt
Born in the U.S.A., Dancing in the Dark, Glory Days, I'm on Fire
dyk: Its seven US Top 10 singles tied the record set by Thriller.

title: The Essential Michael Jackson
starring: Epic / Legacy
runtime: Michael Jackson, Quincy Jones and others
head: The Essential Michael Jackson
craze: Spanning the Jackson 5 to his solo peak, this collection is the go-to introduction to his career. After his death in 2009 it surged back up the charts as a new generation discovered his catalogue.
rows: Michael Jackson, Quincy Jones and others
Billie Jean, Thriller, Man in the Mirror, ABC
dyk: Topped the UK chart for seven weeks in 2009 after Jackson's death.
